text.tspan: Uncertainty propagation: from calibration to vegetation indices, across five optical sensors
Norway field campaign — wheat plots, sub-optimal (variable-cloud) illumination. Each column: one physical instrument.
R per band, per plot ROI
R per band, per plot ROI

⚠ Each instrument below follows its own independent calibration / traceability route to SI — the routes are NOT shared or interchangeable. Only the final reflectance and index values are compared, at the bottom of this diagram.
Cross-sensor intercomparison — reference standard: Piccolo Doppio FLMS
Eₙ ≤ 1 → agreement within combined uncertainty (k=1 ≈ 68% confidence, k=2 ≈ 95%)
Eₙ > 1 → disagreement exceeds what known uncertainty can explain — real bias or missing uncertainty source
Also computed, sensor-vs-Piccolo, across the full spectrum:
Pearson r · regression slope α · intercept (bias) · RMSE
— deviation from the 1:1 identity line quantifies systematic offset between instruments
Validity constraint on every comparison above:
acquisitions must be within ≈ 10 minutes of each other
under variable sky — beyond that, irradiance drift alone can
reach ≈30–34% (90th percentile), swamping any real signal
u_r = random uncertainty · u_s = systematic uncertainty · u_c = combined standard uncertainty · k = coverage factor
